text:
maya: quick heads-up — aurum customer adapter caused weird behaviour after we merged into model-3.1-int4. summarization outputs started hallucinating and there's token-splitting on proprietary doc samples. anyone taking this?

ravi: on it. can you paste adapter id + the eval command you used?

maya: adapter_id: aurum/v1-lora
model: model-3.1
quant: int4
command:
```
./run_eval --model model-3.1 --adapter aurum/v1-lora --quant int4 --tasks summarization,qa --out /tmp/aurum_eval.json
```

eval-bot: automated result: summarization ROUGE-L -12% vs baseline, QA EM -9%, tok_split_rate 0.032 -> 0.12, avg latency +8%. full artifact /evals/2115006789/aurum_eval.json (private).

zack: ran a quick merge + eval in fp16 (no quant) — I don't see hallucinations there. looks like quant interaction.

jen: could be tokenizer subtlety too. did the finetune use any merge ops or token_updates? customer paperwork said they used base tokenizer but i've seen variants where merge rules changed.

ravi: good call. can you repro with tokenizer forced to our canonical vocab? also test with kv-cache off.

maya: repro logs (snip):
```
WARNING tokenizer: unknown_merge_rules detected for aurum/v1-lora
INFO tok_stats: unk_frac=0.004 -> 0.11
SAMPLE_OUTPUT (int4): "The document states that the company acquired... <ILLEGIBLE_SEGMENT> ...more confident claims than source."
```

zack: pushed a temporary routing change: aurum traffic -> model-3.1-fp16 variant until we triage. in prod now (no downtime). created a smoke eval job to compare int8/int4 + adapter-stitch variants. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: queued jobs 2115006795, 2115006812. interim results: int8 shows ROUGE-L -4% (acceptable), int4 still -11%; token_split increases only for int4.

jen: plan: 1) attempt adapter merge with per-layer clipping and weight-norm constraints; 2) run QAT (if feasible) vs PTQ; 3) request customer promptset for targeted regressions. I'll take (1)/(2). @ravi can you secure the promptset?

ravi: yep — i'll DM the secure-bucket link to eng-ml and open a support ticket to ask customer for permission to re-run with QAT. :eyes:

maya: thanks. i'll draft a short incident note and a follow-up action item list for eng-ml weekly. tagging @zack and @jen for postmortem write-up.

zack: odd/interesting case — shows how adapter merges can expose quantization fragility. good signal to add adapter-aware quant checks to our onboarding quickpack.

maya: agreed. will update the onboarding checklist after the triage.
